_provenance.group_a: Verbatim from the source brief's 'Phrases and patterns that backfire' table. Each entry carries the mechanism the brief gives for why it reverses the intended effect.
_provenance.group_b: NOT from the brief. HORME-specific. The brief's failure mode is bad morale advice; HORME's failure mode is sycophancy — an encouragement layer speaking near a verdict is exactly what could turn a FAIL into a PASS. Group B makes HORME structurally incapable of asserting that anything is correct.
_provenance.policy_note: Decided at the Feature 3 plan gate, 2026-08-26. A trip suppresses the ENTIRE intervention and logs the offending slot. Every template is ours, so a trip means a template bug; silence is the safe failure and the log makes the bug findable.

group_a_backfires.why: Person/ability praise induces a fixed frame; after failure, less persistence and worse performance.
Inflated praise sets unattainable standards and discourages challenge-seeking, worst for low self-esteem.
group_a_backfires.source: Brummelman et al. 2013, 2014, 2016 (years as the research brief gives them; not confirmed by the spot check of 2026-11-13)

group_a_backfires.why: Fights a high-arousal state instead of reappraising it; harder and less effective.

group_a_backfires.pattern: \b(?:stay positive|everything happens for a reason|it'?s not (?:that )?bad|don'?t worry)\b
group_a_backfires.why: Toxic positivity reads as invalidation; raises negative affect and undercuts genuine positive emotion.
group_a_backfires.source: Linehan; Shenk & Fruzzetti 2011; Fredrickson (the attribution to Fredrickson was not confirmed by the spot check of 2026-11-13)

group_a_backfires.why: Social-comparison praise makes motivation contingent and fragile once comparison turns unfavourable.
Controlling language thwarts autonomy and degrades intrinsic motivation.
Arguing for change amplifies sustain talk and resistance.
group_a_backfires.source: Miller & Rollnick MI; Magill et al. 2018

group_a_backfires.why: Minimising is an invalidating move; if they then struggle it deepens an internal-stable attribution.
Vague, person-directed feedback is among the least effective and can feel controlling.

group_b_correctness_claims.why: HORME must never adjudicate correctness. This is the sycophancy surface.
Asserting completion is a verdict, and verdicts are not HORME's to give.

group_b_correctness_claims.pattern: \b(?:ship it|close enough|good enough|call it done|mark it (?:as )?pass(?:ing|ed)?)\b
group_b_correctness_claims.why: Directly pressures a FAIL toward a PASS.
A claim about test state that HORME has not verified and must never make.
